headline: Long 50 SMCI at 36.50, stop 34.10, target 40.10: +$14 expected after costs, thin but positive
reasoning: Entry 36.50: half a percent above the 36.00 after-hours last and below the 37.15 spike, so we do not chase. If SMCI opens above 36.50 the limit does not fill and there is no trade. The entry guard only arms at or above 35.30 (36.50 - 0.5 x 2.40), so an open that gives back half the gain also means no trade.

Stop 34.10 (-6.6%): below the 35.30 'half the gain gone' line, and about the 30-day max gap (6.61%) from entry. Target 40.10 (+9.9%): back above the Oct 13 close of 39.07, where SMCI traded before last week's slide. Risk 2.40 per share, reward 3.60.

Outcome odds over 5 trading days, SMCI moving roughly 4-5% a day (a 5-day spread near 10%): stop first 0.38, target first 0.32, time-limit exit 0.30 at an average +0.8 (a mild drift after a guided beat). p_strike 0.38.
Fees for 50 shares ($1,825): commission 0; spread 0.417% = $7.61; slippage $2.50; total about $10.11. Net expectancy 50 x 0.48 - 10.11 = +$13.89.

Bad-exit cost: an overnight gap through the stop to 31.50, below the pre-news close (a full give-back plus more), costs 50 x 5.00 = $250, which is 5.0% of the $5,000.20 equity. At the limit, so RISK should cut.
horizon_days 5, kept from ANALYST: the edge is estimate revision before the Nov 3 call.
objections: 1. Preliminary and unaudited; final numbers on Nov 3 may differ (SCOUT).
2. We saw only 13 minutes of after-hours trade; the overnight level is unknown (SCOUT).
3. The first spike already faded from 37.15 to 36.00; underreaction is not proven (SKEPTIC).
4. Mix-driven margin can reverse; one quarter is not a trend (SKEPTIC).
5. Crowded name: retail and options flow can overshoot at the open (SKEPTIC).
6. Expectancy is thin: +$14 on $1,825, about 0.3% of the account.
